insurer: Niva Bupa Health Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: Base Sum Insured options: ₹1L / ₹2L / ₹3L / ₹4L / ₹5L / ₹7.5L / ₹10L / ₹15L / ₹25L (Policy Schedule will show chosen SI). Re-fill up to 100% of Base SI. Optional I-Protect increases SI by 10% of Base SI each renewal if opted.

great.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
great.quote: We will not be liable to pay Pre-hospitalization Medical Expenses for more than 90 days immediately preceding the Insured Person’s admission
great.explanation: Pre-hospitalization medical expenses are covered for up to 90 days before admission. This is longer than many plans and helps pay for consultations, tests, and medicines leading up to hospitalization.

good.name: Restore Benefit
good.quote: We will provide a Re-fill amount of maximum up to 100% of the Base Sum Insured
good.explanation: A refill of up to 100% of the Base Sum Insured is available after the base sum insured is used. This increases your available cover for additional hospitalizations in the same policy year.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a Pre-existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first Policy.
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are covered only after 36 months of continuous coverage from the first policy inception. This means PED-related claims are not payable during the first 3 years.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first Policy.
good.explanation: Listed specific illnesses/surgeries are covered only after 24 months of continuous coverage from the first policy inception. This means you must wait 2 years before claiming for those listed conditions.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any Illness within 30 days from the first Policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an Accident
good.explanation: Illness-related claims are not covered for the first 30 days from policy start, while accidents are covered immediately. This is a standard waiting period in retail health insurance.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: We will not be liable to pay Post-hospitalization Medical Expenses for more than 180 days immediately following the Insured Person’s discharge from Hospital
good.explanation: Post-hospitalization medical expenses are covered for up to 180 days after discharge. This helps pay for follow-up consultations, tests, and medicines after hospitalization.

good.name: Domiciliary Hospitalization
good.quote: We will indemnify on a Reimbursement basis the Medical Expenses incurred for Domiciliary Hospitalization... The Home Health Care Services are covered only if We have accepted a claim under Section 3.1 (Inpatient Care) above and Home Health Care Services are availed immediately after that Hospitalization.
good.explanation: Domiciliary hospitalization expenses are reimbursed when treatment is taken at home as per the policy terms, and home health care is covered only after an accepted inpatient claim and immediately after discharge. This can help when continued care is needed at home, but it is conditional on a prior approved hospitalization claim.

bad.name: Room Rent
bad.quote: Room Rent (per day) Up to 1% of Base Sum Insured
bad.reference: Annexure IV (Product Benefit Table) – Room Rent (per day) for 1 lac / 2 lacs
bad.explanation: Room rent is capped at 1% of the Base Sum Insured per day. If you choose a room costing more than this limit, your claim payout can reduce significantly.

bad.name: Proportionate Deduction
bad.quote: We shall be liable to pay only a pro-rated portion of the total Associated Medical Expenses... in the proportion of the difference between the Room Rent actually incurred and the Room Rent specified in the Policy Schedule
bad.explanation: If you stay in a room above the eligible room rent, the insurer pays associated medical expenses only in the same proportion as the room rent shortfall. This can sharply increase your out-of-pocket costs beyond just the room rent difference.

bad.name: Restore Benefit
bad.quote: The re-fill amount may be used for only subsequent claims... and shall not be for any Illness / Injury (including its complications or follow up) for which a claim has been paid or accepted as payable in the current Policy Year for the same Insured Person.
bad.explanation: The refill amount cannot be used for the same illness/injury (including complications or follow-ups) if a claim for it has already been paid/accepted in the same policy year for the same person. This limits refill usefulness for repeated admissions for one ongoing condition.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: ANNEXURE II – List I – Expenses not covered... 56 GLOVES ... 60 MASK ... 58 ANY KIT WITH NO DETAILS MENTIONED [DELIVERY KIT, ORTHOKIT, RECOVERY KIT, ETC]
bad.reference: Annexure II (List I – Expenses not covered)
bad.explanation: Common consumables like gloves, masks and various kits are listed as not covered. These items are frequently billed by hospitals and can add to your non-payable expenses.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: Co-payment (if applicable) as specified in the Policy Schedule shall be applicable on the amount payable by Us.
bad.explanation: A co-pay can apply as per the Policy Schedule, meaning you may have to bear a percentage of each claim. This directly increases your share of costs even when the claim is otherwise admissible.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
